name: Dull Blue
lede: Dull Blue is a muted, mid-dark blue, an everyday descriptive name for a blue with little vividness.

sections.title: A plain description
sections.body:
Our earliest record of Dull Blue as a color name is the xkcd list of 2010 [3]. The words are older. Ruskin remarked of a Rubens landscape that the rainbow was a dull blue, darker than the sky [1]. Gurney says the white letters of an old neon sign, where they fall in shadow, are really a dull blue-gray [2]. Paterson defines gunmetal as the dull blue-grey colour of the metal, a dark grey, and records the variant name gunmetal blue [4]. That makes dull blue a long-standing way to describe a muted, greyed blue, even though the name as a swatch is recent [3][4].

Its nearest neighbors among our names, by CIELAB distance, are [[stardew|Stardew]], [[stormy-blue|Stormy Blue]] and [[queen-blue|Queen Blue]] [5]. On a white page it reaches a contrast ratio of 4.87:1 [5].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Dull Blue appears in 139 of 23,781 paintings, 0.58%, as photographed [6]. It most often plays an accent, in 52% of the 64 paintings where the within-painting reading finds it [6]. It peaks in the 1900s at 2.3 times the expected rate (13 paintings) [6]. The earliest match is a work by Colart de Laon from 1405; the early centuries are thin, so that is a floor and not a first [6].
